newsitem.title: UK: China's Datang debuts on London Stock Exchange.
newsitem.headline: China's Datang debuts on London Stock Exchange.

text.p: Beijing Datang Power Generation on Monday made its market debut as the first Chinese company to have its shares quoted in London.
Datang, one of China's largest independent electric power producers, raised over HK$3 billion ($387.4 million) in an international equity offering.
The issue, brought to the market by investment banks Morgan Stanley and Dresdner Kleinwort Benson, was heavily oversubcribed.

"We are delighted to welcome Datang to the Exchange. Its listing illustrates that Chinese companies are aware of the strengths of London's financial market and the role the Exchange can play in enabling them to raise capital," the London Stock Exchange said.

Jiao Yian, Chairman of Datang, Zhou Daojiong, Chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission and Ma Zhengang, the new Chinese Ambassador were welcomed to the Exchange by Chairman John Kemp-Welch to mark the occasion.
